target_customer: Women in their 20s and 30s who are not ready for children yet and pay out of pocket for at-home hormone testing
problem: Fertility hormone testing was mostly confined to clinics and costly, so women had little early information about their reproductive health. Modern Fertility sold a mail-order finger-prick and blood test that reported hormone levels with doctor-reviewed results.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer test kits sold per order, later adding ovulation and pregnancy tests and a membership app
product_category: Consumer health, at-home diagnostics, women's health

founders.name: Afton Vechery
founders.background_notes: Per press she started the company after paying over $1,500 for fertility testing herself.

founders.name: Carly Leahy
founders.background_notes: Described in press as the brand builder of the company.

competitors.name: Everlywell
competitors.what: At-home lab test kits including a fertility panel testing a wider range of hormones

technical_complexity.rationale: Relied on partner labs and an existing finger-prick collection method, so the hard parts were clinical validation, physician network and logistics rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Kits and lab partners were available to rivals; differentiation was price, brand and the growing dataset of results, which a later app aimed to deepen.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large incumbent copied it in the early years. In May 2021 telehealth company Ro acquired it for a reported 225 million dollars, mostly in stock.

market_need_then: Women reported paying well over a thousand dollars and waiting for clinic referrals to learn basic fertility hormone levels, while egg freezing and delayed childbearing were growing topics in 2017.

branding.domain_note: Used modernfertility.com; the domain now redirects to ro.co after the 2021 acquisition.

identity.visual_style: Clean, clinical but warm consumer look; packaging deliberately avoided baby imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Empowering and informative, aimed at women planning ahead rather than trying to conceive now

branding.brand_signature: Fertility packaging with no baby imagery, framing fertility as personal information rather than only motherhood
branding.community_and_virality: Strong early press and a reported waitlist and fast growth; the CCO was described as a brand builder. No specific merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well covered in press and recognized in women's health, with a distinct no baby imagery stance, but the name is descriptive and the brand was folded into Ro after four years.

outcome_analysis: Modern Fertility rode growing interest in proactive women's health and sold a low-cost hormone test with strong consumer press, raising a 15 million dollar Series A from Forerunner in 2019. It reached a reported acquisition by Ro for about 225 million dollars in May 2021 within four years of launch. After the deal the CEO left around a year later, and the brand was absorbed into Ro's women's health line.
notes: YC page says 22 million raised, but only the 15 million Series A is confirmed by a second outlet. A roughly 1 million 2017 angel round and a roughly 6 million 2018 seed appear in aggregators only and are unverified, so the seed amount is left null. Totals vary from 21 to 23 million across aggregators. Union Square Ventures is named on the YC page but not confirmed elsewhere. Competitor list is limited to those named in 2017 coverage. Website redirects to ro.co/fertility.
